S43.01.needs: a vision-capable model selected with /model, an image file
S43.01.note: Whether the model's answer is correct is not checked here; I only traced that the image is staged and sent with the next message.
steps: Start agi and pick a vision-capable model with /model (agi refuses images on a model that does not accept them, with the text "switch to a vision model with /model first").
Type /attach followed by the path to a PNG or JPG on your Mac, and press Enter.
Look for the message "Attached <name> (<size>). It goes with your next message; /attach remove drops it."
Type a question about the picture (for example "What is in this image?") and send.
Compare the reply with Expected: it should answer about the picture you attached.
S43.01.where: agi, then type /attach <path to image>, then type your question and send

S43.02.needs: a vision-capable model selected with /model, two image files
S43.02.note: apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs has a max images per request value, and I did not confirm the TUI enforces it when more than one image is staged.
steps: Start agi with a vision-capable model selected by /model.
Type /attach <first image path> and press Enter, then type /attach <second image path> and press Enter.
Type /attach list and press Enter. Look for "Staged for the next turn:" with both images numbered 1 and 2.
Type a message such as "Compare these two images" and send.
Compare with Expected: the reply should describe both images and how they differ.
S43.02.where: agi, then /attach <image 1>, then /attach <image 2>, then /attach list to check

S43.03.needs: a vision-capable model selected with /model, a screenshot on the clipboard
S43.03.note: Only the clipboard path is coded for a captured or pasted screenshot; I did not find a separate screenshot-capture command in apps/cli.
steps: Take a screenshot so it is on the clipboard, then start agi with a vision-capable model selected by /model.
Press Ctrl+V in the message box. The status line should show "attached clipboard (<width>x<height>)".
Type /attach list and press Enter to confirm the screenshot is staged.
Type "What does this screenshot show?" and send.
Compare with Expected: the reply should explain what the screenshot shows.
S43.03.where: agi, then Ctrl+V in the message box (or /attach clipboard after copying a screenshot)

Type "Read this document and explain it" and send.

S43.08.needs: a vision-capable model selected with /model, an image containing text
S43.08.note: I found no dedicated OCR command or copy button; I searched apps/cli/src for "ocr" and "extract text" images, and text extraction is only the model's reply. The typed command in where has a stray brace; the actual command is /attach <path to an image containing text>.
steps: Start agi and select a vision-capable model with /model.
Type /attach <path to an image containing text> and press Enter.
Type "Extract all the text in this image exactly." and send.
Select the returned text in the terminal with the mouse, copy it, and compare with Expected: the copied text should match the text in the image.

S43.18.needs: a vision-capable model selected with /model, a large detailed image
S43.18.note: The code has two modes only: scaled to fit by default and full resolution with --full (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs and apps/cli/src/lib.rs). The words high-detail and reduced-detail do not appear in the CLI; I did not trace the size the model actually receives, so end-to-end honouring is unverified.
steps: Start agi and select a vision-capable model with /model.
Type /attach <path to a large, detailed image> and press Enter. Note the message "Attached <name> (<size>). It goes with your next message; /attach remove drops it."
Type /attach remove all, then type /attach --full <same image path> and press Enter.
Look for the message "It is sent without being scaled down, so it costs more input".
Compare with Expected: the full-resolution attach should be the only one that says it is not scaled down, and the reply should show more detail when asked about fine text.
S43.18.where: agi, then /attach --full <image path> and compare with /attach <image path>
